Modern translations registered on SuttaCentral include an English version by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
No independent parallels are curated on SuttaCentral, but automated analysis by DharmaNexus documents substantial text reuse within the Pali canon and across Buddhist languages [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies 1,635 matching passages shared across 71 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest internal reuse occurs with other analytical matrices within the *Parivāra*, including another homonymous *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 1.2, sharing extensive portions such as §7.4–18.4 with §7.2–18.4), the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 2.10 and Pvr 1.9), the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4), *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 2.2), *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11), and both *Samuccayavāra* sections (Pvr 1.16 and Pvr 2.16) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, it shares substantial formulaic phrasing with the *Suttavibhaṅga* (such as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 1 and Pārājika 3, as well as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pārājika 5) and with post-canonical treatises such as the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus link the text with Vinaya and lexicographical material in Sanskrit and Tibetan, including the Sanskrit *Mahāvyutpatti*, the Tibetan *Prātimokṣasūtra* (D0002), the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007A), the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122), and Gunaprabha's *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120-2) [DharmaNexus].
